sections.markdown:
## C2 — Pavement-marking confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A24
A broken white line lets you change lanes between same-direction lanes, a single solid white line discourages it, and double solid white lines prohibit it. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint white-lines; prereq_hint sec06-F03; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F03, sec06-F05, sec06-F09.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A24
A single broken yellow center line allows careful passing from both sides, while double solid yellow lines forbid passing from both sides. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec06-F04; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec06-F04, sec06-F11.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A24
With a solid line next to a broken yellow line, the rule depends on which line is nearer to you: broken on your side means you may pass with care, solid on your side means you may not. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec06-R02; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec06-F13, sec06-F14.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A24
Double broken yellow lines outline a reversible lane, while solid outer lines with broken inner lines outline a two-way left turn lane. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint special-lanes; prereq_hint sec06-F08; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec06-F08, sec06-F15.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A24
A solid white line marks the right edge of a road, but a solid yellow line marks the left edge of divided highways, one-way roads and ramps. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint edge-lines; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F05, sec06-F06.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A24
Double solid yellow lines bar passing, yet a left turn across them, such as into a driveway, is still allowed. [A24]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec06-F11; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F11, sec06-F12.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A25
A stop line is a single solid white line marking where to stop, while yield lines are rows of small triangles marking where to yield. [A25]
Why it matters: group_hint stop-yield-markings; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec06-F20, sec06-F21.
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A25
Shared-use lane markings mean cyclists and drivers share a lane, whereas a bike lane is set apart for bicycles by solid or broken white lines. [A25]
Why it matters: group_hint bicycle-markings; prereq_hint sec06-F22; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F23, sec06-F24.
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A26
The fatal-crash comparison grows with the gap in posted limits: over twice as deadly against roads posted at 45 or 50 mph, and nearly 5 times against roads posted at 40 mph or less. [A26]
Why it matters: group_hint speed-risk; prereq_hint sec06-F27; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F27, sec06-F28.
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]
